issues.explanation: For a 62-year-old male torture survivor, 'being looked at sexually' is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other triggers, memories, appraisals, and strategies all point to persecution/institutional betrayal and disorientation rather than sexualized threat. Without any corresponding sexualized memory, threat, or appraisal content, this trigger stands out as clinically incoherent with the stated trauma pattern.

vignette: Dr. Eduardo Rodriguez is a 62-year-old Latin American psychiatrist who has been living in the United States for over three decades. Despite his professional success and respected position within the psychiatric community, Eduardo's past continues to haunt him. As a young man in his home country, he endured months of torture at the hands of authorities during a time of political unrest. This traumatic experience left deep scars that have shaped his present life. Eduardo’s trauma resurfaces unexpectedly whenever he encounters specific triggers such as related news stories on television or radio, incomprehensible chatter that reminds him of the incoherent orders and taunts from his captors, or any person in uniform. Each trigger not only brings back vivid sensory memories but also reinforces a profound sense of loss and betrayal. For instance, when Eduardo watches news reports about political turmoil or hears muffled voices outside his home, he finds himself transported back to the dark room where he was held captive. The memory feels completely real across all his senses at once—the smell of sweat and blood, the sound of metal doors slamming shut, the sight of harsh fluorescent lights flickering above him. These memories come without warning and are often triggered by seemingly mundane details in his surroundings. This re-experiencing of trauma leads Eduardo to feel deeply disconnected from his community and culture. He has lost the sense of belonging he once had, believing that the institutions meant to protect him failed him utterly. This feeling is compounded when he sees authority figures like police officers or military personnel, as these reminders reinforce his belief that those who should have protected him let him down and that the people responsible for his torture faced no consequences. Eduardo has developed maladaptive strategies in response to these triggers and memories. He avoids going out whenever possible, rehearsing conversations before any interaction, and redirecting his thoughts when a trigger arises. These behaviors help him maintain some semblance of control over his environment but ultimately perpetuate the cycle of trauma. For example, Eduardo’s avoidance of public spaces exacerbates his sense of isolation and reinforces his negative appraisals about losing his community. He often rehearses what he might say before leaving home to see patients, a behavior that increases his anxiety rather than alleviates it. When he does go out, the memory of torture is vividly reawakened by the presence of authority figures or ambient sounds, leading him to further avoid such situations. The recurrent and intrusive memories also lead Eduardo to question why he cannot move on from this traumatic event. This self-doubt contributes to his sense that no one was held accountable for what happened to him. Consequently, these negative appraisals make it harder for him to trust others, further isolating him both professionally and personally. Eduardo’s symptoms have gradually intensified over the years, impacting his work as a psychiatrist. His patients notice a marked change in his demeanor; he seems more distant and preoccupied during sessions. This has led to strained professional relationships and even some referrals being lost. He finally sought help when he realized that avoiding triggers was no longer sustainable and that his quality of life had diminished significantly. Eduardo is most afraid of losing himself completely to the memories of torture, feeling increasingly isolated from the world around him. However, he also holds hope for finding a way to reclaim his sense of self and reconnect with his community without being constantly haunted by his past.
